The top band is thin and could be read as the top of the backrest rather than a seat surface, so the seat surface itself is hidden from this angle. styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts are close to the references: 13 distinct colours against 14 for the bench, 0% flat-fill coverage, and only 8% neutral dark edge pixels. So the outline is a tinted dark blue-grey, not a neutral black sticker line, and nothing is a large flat fill. By eye the piece still looks shallow. It is a stiff, symmetric grey block (it reads almost like a robot or a statue) with only about 3 lightness steps per material: a light face, a mid face and a dark edge. It has little grain, per-surface highlighting or material variation, whereas the bench, stall and well show 5-6 steps with highlights, wood grain and individually shaded parts. The form also reads poorly as a reclining seat seen from behind. Set beside the references it looks flatter and less crafted, so I fail it on shading depth and texture even though the numbers are acceptable.
